anomalies.description: A sudden, intense bright flash erupts behind a structure, rapidly expanding into a large fireball with visible shockwave-like expansion and ejection of incandescent debris (sparks/fragments) outward—characteristic of a high-energy explosion.

A large, bright orange fireball erupts with a dense shower of incandescent sparks radiating outward, consistent with a high-energy explosion (e.g., pyrotechnic or munition detonation). The initial blast is most intense at f0–f2 and rapidly expands and dissipates through f3–f4.

Following the initial blast, a sustained secondary phase shows vigorous ejection of numerous hot particles/sparks in an upward and outward trajectory, with the core fireball diminishing but still glowing intensely—indicative of post-detonation fragmentation and combustion of explosive material or secondary fuel.

Following the initial blast, a sustained fiery plume rises and evolves, with residual sparks and glowing embers visible through f5–f15. This represents the after-effect phase of the same explosive event—burning debris and hot gases rising—rather than a separate explosion. The luminous core remains visible and gradually fades.
